newsitem.title: FRANCE: Council of Europe urges eradicating child labour.
newsitem.headline: Council of Europe urges eradicating child labour.

text.p: The Council of Europe parliamentary assembly urged its 40 member states on Thursday to eradicate the exploitation of children through labour or prostitution.
The assembly, citing statistics from the International Labour Organisation. noted that 250 million of the world's children work, about of them full-time.
Michel Hansenne, director of the ILO's executive body said that while child labour was most prevalent in developing countries, children were also exploited in industrialised European states.

He told the assembly the ILO's conference next year would propose a draft convention to tighten the 1973 convention which bans employing children under 15 and dangerous jobs for those under 18. The convention has only been ratified by 51 states.
A report adopted by the assembly said that half the children aged 13 to 15 in Britain had some sort of part-time work and child prostitution was a major problem among orphans or homeless children.
In Spain and in Italy, 1.5 million children are employed, while two million children work in family businesses in Turkey, the report said.
It stressed the condition of gypsy children in certain countries who are forced into theft and prostitution.
The assembly urged the member states to re-evaluate existing legislation to better protect children.
